<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Overview</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Synergetics USA, Inc. (&#8220;Synergetics USA&#8221; or &#8220;the Company&#8221;) is a leading supplier of precision surgical devices. The Company&#8217;s primary focus is on the disciplines of ophthalmology and neurosurgery. Our distribution channels include a combination of direct and independent distributor sales organizations, both domestically and internationally, and important strategic alliances with market leaders. The Company&#8217;s product lines focus upon precision engineered, disposable and reusable devices, surgical equipment, surgical procedural kits and the delivery of various energy modalities for the performance of surgery, including: (i) laser energy, (ii) ultrasonic energy, (iii) radio frequency energy for electrosurgery and lesion generation and (iv) visible light energy for illumination, and where applicable, simultaneous infusion (irrigation) of fluids into the operative field. Enterprise-wide sales information is included in Note 17 to the audited consolidated financial statements filed as a part of this Annual Report on Form 10-K.</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Company is a Delaware corporation incorporated on June 2, 2005, in connection with the reverse merger of Synergetics, Inc. (&#8220;Synergetics&#8221;) and Valley Forge Scientific Corp. (&#8220;Valley Forge&#8221;) and the subsequent reincorporation of Valley Forge (the predecessor to Synergetics USA) in Delaware.&#160; Synergetics was founded in 1991. Valley Forge was incorporated in 1980 and became a publicly-held company in November 1989.&#160; The Company&#8217;s securities are listed on The NASDAQ Capital Market under the ticker symbol &#8220;SURG.&#8221;</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Recent Developments</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">We had several developments since fiscal 2012 that we expect will contribute to the growth of our business in the foreseeable future.</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">On October 27, 2011, the Company announced two new ophthalmic products for the vitrectomy market which were showcased at the 2011 Annual Meeting of the American Academy of Ophthalmology.&#160; The Company also announced record sales leads generated from the showcasing of its ophthalmic products.</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">On December 31, 2011, the Company&#8217;s agreements with Codman &amp; Shurtleff, Inc. (&#8220;Codman&#8221;) were renewed for a period of three years.</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">On February 9, 2012, Mobius Therapeutics, LLC, a St. Louis-based ophthalmic pharmaceutical company, announced that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (&#8220;FDA&#8221;) had approved its orphan drug for glaucoma and that Synergetics would be manufacturing the kit for the administration of the drug.</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">On June 27, 2012, the Company announced that it received 510(k) clearance from the FDA for VersaVIT<sup style="vertical-align: text-top; line-height: 1; font-size: smaller;">TM</sup>, a novel vitrectomy system for the retinal surgery market.&#160; On July 20, 2012, the VersaVIT<sup style="vertical-align: text-top; line-height: 1; font-size: smaller;">TM</sup> vitrectomy system received clearance for the &#8220;CE&#8221; mark, allowing access to the European market.</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">On November 28, 2012, the Company announced the signing of the third amendment to its agreement with Stryker Corporation (&#8220;Stryker&#8221;) for the supply and distribution of a multi-channel ablation generator and accessories, used for minimally invasive pain treatment, extending the termination date until June 30, 2015.</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">On July 9, 2013, the Company announced that it acquired M.I.S.S. Ophthalmics Limited (&#8220;M.I.S.S.&#8221;), a private ophthalmology distribution company incorporated in England and Wales, for net cash consideration of $2.8 million.</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">On September 30, 2013, the Company extended its revolving credit facility and its equipment line of credit through September 30, 2016.</div>

<div style="MARGIN-TOP: 10pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 10pt; CLEAR: both" id="DSPFPageBreakArea">
<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: right; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', Times, Serif; FONT-SIZE: 8pt" id="DSPFPageNumberArea">3</div>

<hr style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: always; BORDER-RIGHT-WIDTH: 0px; BACKGROUND-COLOR: #000000; MARGIN: 4px 0px; WIDTH: 100%; BORDER-TOP-WIDTH: 0px; BORDER-BOTTOM-WIDTH: 0px; HEIGHT: 2px; COLOR: #000000; CLEAR: both; BORDER-LEFT-WIDTH: 0px" id="DSPFPageBreak" noshade="noshade">
<div style="WIDTH: 100%" id="DSPFPageHeader">
<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 8pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal"><a href="#TABLEOFCONTENTS">Table of Contents</a></div>
</div>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">On October 1, 2013, the Company announced plans to close its King of Prussia, Pennsylvania facility and consolidate the manufacturing operations into its existing facility in O&#8217;Fallon, Missouri.&#160; The Company expects to expense approximately $1.2 million, of which $682,000 was expended during fiscal 2014.&#160; The remaining approximately $500,000 will be expended over the next five months to complete the closure. The Company expects the closure to result in a reduction in operating expense of more than $1.1 million on an annualized basis beginning in fiscal 2016.</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">On May 3, 2014, the Company acquired a private original equipment manufacturing (&#8220;OEM&#8221;) company incorporated in the United States for net cash consideration of $1.4 million.</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">On May 5, 2014, the Company announced the launch of the next generation Directional<sup style="vertical-align: text-top; line-height: 1; font-size: smaller;">TM</sup> Laser Probe.&#160; The Directional<sup style="vertical-align: text-top; line-height: 1; font-size: smaller;">TM</sup> II Laser Probe is a significant improvement as compared to the original Directional<sup style="vertical-align: text-top; line-height: 1; font-size: smaller;">TM</sup> Laser Probe as it incorporates years of feedback from surgeons on the original design.&#160; The improvements include an ergonomic, color-coded handle that emulates our Pinnacle<sup style="vertical-align: text-top; line-height: 1; font-size: smaller;">TM</sup> instrument line and significant enhancements to the mechanism responsible for adjusting the fiber from a straight to curved position.</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">On May 12, 2014, the Company announced the completion of a cooperative development agreement with Cleveland Clinic to develop the next generation of intraoperative devices.&#160; These devices are expected to lead to improved visualization of surgical sites leading to more precise tissue targeting and improved surgical outcomes.</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">On June 9, 2014, the Company announced the targeted launch of the next generation vitrectomy system, VersaVIT 2.0<sup style="vertical-align: text-top; line-height: 1; font-size: smaller;">TM</sup>, in the second-half of June.&#160; VersaVIT 2.0<sup style="vertical-align: text-top; line-height: 1; font-size: smaller;">TM</sup> offers an improvement over the first generation system by providing high speed cutting in combination with active duty cycle control. Combined, both high speed cutting and duty cycle control provide surgeons with a more efficient way to remove vitreous while simultaneously increasing safety by decreasing traction on retinal tissues when shaving along the base of the retina. Additional features of the VersaVIT 2.0&#8482; system and accessories include LED illumination, pressurized infusion and a silicone oil collection chamber.</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Non-GAAP Financial Measures</div>

<div>&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt">We measure our performance primarily through our operating profit.&#160; In addition to our audited consolidated financial statements presented in accordance with GAAP, management uses certain non-GAAP measures, including EBITDA, operating return on average equity and operating return on average assets, to measure our operating performance.&#160; We provide a definition of the components of these measurements and reconciliation to the most directly comparable GAAP financial measure.</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt">These non-GAAP measures are presented to enhance an understanding of our operating results and are not intended to represent cash flow or results of operations.&#160; The use of these non-GAAP measures provides an indication of our ability to service debt and measure operating performance.&#160; We believe these non-GAAP measures are useful in evaluating our operating performance compared to other companies in our industry, and are beneficial to investors, potential investors and other key stakeholders, including creditors who use this measure in their evaluation of performance.</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt">These non-GAAP measures are not in accordance with, or an alternative to, measures prepared in accordance with GAAP and may be different from non-GAAP measures used by other companies.&#160; In addition, these non-GAAP measures are not based on any comprehensive set of accounting rules or principles.&#160; Non-GAAP measures have limitations in that they do not reflect all of the amounts associated with the Company&#8217;s results of operations as determined in accordance with GAAP.&#160; These measures should only be used to evaluate our results of operations in conjunction with the corresponding GAAP measures.</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Our Business Strategy</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Company&#8217;s strategy is to enhance shareholder value through profitable revenue growth in targeted segments of the ophthalmology and neurosurgery markets. This is accomplished through the identification and development of reusable and disposable devices in collaboration with leading surgeons and OEM partners. We are committed to establishing a strong operational infrastructure and financial foundation within which growth opportunities can be prudently evaluated, financed and pursued. We will remain vigilant and sensitive to new challenges which may arise from changes in the definition and delivery of appropriate healthcare in our fields of interest. In fiscal 2015 and beyond, our strategic priorities are to drive accelerating growth in the ophthalmology business, deliver improved profitability through our enterprise-wide continuous improvement initiatives, manage our neurosurgery and other OEM businesses for stable growth and strong cash flows, demonstrate consistent, solid financial performance and continued growth through strategic acquisitions.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">
<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-STYLE: italic; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Drive Accelerating Growth in our Ophthalmology Business</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">We are focused on expanding our product platform into larger and faster-growing segments of the vitreoretinal device market. Thus, we have focused our internal research and development efforts on developing innovative technologies that will enable the Company to enhance its value to the vitreoretinal community. We are implementing several focused initiatives to leverage on our recent introduction of VersaVIT 2.0<font size="2"><font style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><sup style="vertical-align: text-top; line-height: 1; font-size: smaller;">TM</sup></font> and other new products to capitalize on the current macroeconomic environment.<font style="FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#160;</font>In addition, we are also seeking business development opportunities to augment and complement our existing ophthalmic franchise.&#160; Finally, we are improving our sales force productivity. For example, in the U.S., we are focused on enhancing our compensation programs to target the appropriate mix of product. Also, we are focused on rigorous development of our sales force capabilities through enhanced training and customer relationship management. In the international markets, we are working to optimize our sales capabilities and distribution infrastructure.&#160; Our recent acquisition of M.I.S.S. demonstrates our commitment to enhancing our international distribution infrastructure.</font></div>
</div>

<div style="MARGIN-TOP: 10pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 10pt; CLEAR: both" id="DSPFPageBreakArea">
<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: right; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', Times, Serif; FONT-SIZE: 8pt" id="DSPFPageNumberArea">6</div>

<div style="WIDTH: 100%" id="DSPFPageHeader">
<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 8pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal"><a href="#TABLEOFCONTENTS">Table of Contents</a></div>
</div>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-STYLE: italic; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Deliver Improved Profitability through our Enterprise-Wide Continuous Improvement Initiatives</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">We have been developing comprehensive enterprise-wide continuous improvement initiatives aimed at creating a more efficient operating platform. We implemented our Enterprise Resource Planning (&#8220;ERP&#8221;) system in August 2011 which brought us accurate, timely information to more effectively manage our cost savings initiatives.&#160; Prior to fiscal 2014, we believe we have taken over $2.0 million out of our cost basis since we implemented our cost savings efforts.&#160; Through reducing our scrap, more efficient use of our labor force and concentrating our efforts on less costly components, we believe we have saved another $1.1 million in fiscal 2014.&#160; Also, during fiscal 2014, we began our efforts to consolidate our manufacturing operations in O&#8217;Fallon, Missouri.&#160; We believe these efforts will result in an additional $1.1 million in operating savings on an annualized basis beginning in fiscal 2016.</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-STYLE: italic; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Manage our Neurosurgery and OEM Businesses for Stable Growth and Strong Cash Flows</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">We have long-term relationships established with our two largest OEM partners, Codman and Stryker. These relationships provide high visibility within the neurosurgery and pain control markets. We provide best-in-class technologies with our electrosurgical generators and disposable bipolar forceps being distributed by Codman and our multi-channel ablation generator and ultrasonic aspirator disposables being distributed by Stryker. We are working with both of these OEM partners to provide product line iterations to maintain their technological advantages. We also work with a select number of other potential OEM customers to develop relationships to support our strategic goal.</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-STYLE: italic; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Demonstrate Consistent, Solid Financial Performance</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In the short and long-term, we expect to grow our revenues and increase our profitability. We also will enhance our working capital usages by employing both our enterprise-wide continuous improvement initiatives and our ERP system to derive more free cash flow from the business. We will prudently manage our capital structure to allow for additional growth opportunities and optimal cash deployment.</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-STYLE: italic; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Continued Growth through Strategic Acquisitions</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-STYLE: italic; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">We believe that we can generate substantial revenue and cost synergies through strategic acquisitions and have a history of successfully acquiring and integrating companies that expand our footprint, either geographically or in market sectors that are complementary to our existing operations.&#160; We intend to continue to grow our business and enhance our product offerings through acquisitions that either complement our existing products or provide additional resources or products that will enrich and increase our customer relationships.&#160; We regularly consider and enter into discussions regarding potential acquisitions. Any such transaction would be subject to negotiation of mutually agreeable terms and conditions, receipt of fairness opinions (if required) and approval of the parties&#8217; respective boards of directors and can be effected quickly, may occur at any time and may be significant in size relative to our existing assets or operations.</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Research and Development (&#8220;R&amp;D&#8221;) Strategy</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Our R&amp;D strategy primarily focuses on developing new products in collaboration with leading retinal surgeons and our OEM partners utilizing our proprietary technology and our expertise in vitreoretinal surgery and neurosurgery.&#160; We are continually engineering new products, systems and instrumentation, as well as enhancements to existing products, to meet the needs of surgeons in the ophthalmology and neurosurgery disciplines.&#160; We have entered into consultation arrangements with leading ophthalmic surgeons, all of whom specialize in vitreoretinal procedures.&#160; In neurosurgery, we have worked closely with our OEM partners to develop ultrasonic aspirator tips and other handheld devices.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Company has historically invested in specific R&amp;D projects.&#160; In fiscal 2014, we spent approximately 80 percent of our R&amp;D expenditures on ophthalmic opportunities and 20 percent on neurosurgery and other OEM opportunities.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 14.4pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">At July 31, 2014, the Company&#8217;s development pipeline included 24 active projects in various stages of completion.&#160; The Company completed its most recent top priority ophthalmology R&amp;D project when it introduced the&#160;enhanced VersaVIT 2.0<font style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><sup style="vertical-align: text-top; line-height: 1; font-size: smaller;">TM</sup></font> vitrectomy machine for use in vitreoretinal procedures. The launch of this product strengthens the Company&#8217;s position in the estimated annual $336 million vitrectomy machine and $215 million related procedural pack markets. We have begun development work on several of the larger active projects which are a subset of the 24 which we believe will drive future growth in both our ophthalmic and neurosurgery businesses.&#160; In fiscal 2015, our key objective is to continue to commercialize VersaVIT 2.0<sup style="vertical-align: text-top; line-height: 1; font-size: smaller;">TM </sup>globally.</div>

<div><br>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Company expects to invest in R&amp;D at a rate of approximately 6 to 8 percent of net sales each fiscal year.&#160;&#160;The majority&#160;of our R&amp;D is conducted internally.&#160; In fiscal 2015, we expect to fund all of our R&amp;D projects with current assets and cash flows from operations.&#160; We continuously review our R&amp;D initiatives to ensure they remain consistent with and supportive of our strategic growth initiatives.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Marketing</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Ophthalmic/Vitreoretinal</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="BACKGROUND-COLOR: #ffffff">
<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Markets</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 9pt">&#160;</div>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 24.5pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Vitreoretinal surgery refers to any surgical procedures involving the posterior portion of the eye, also commonly referred to as &#8220;the back of the eye.&#8221; Conditions associated with vitreoretinal surgery often require surgical treatment to prevent vision loss. These conditions include proliferative diabetic retinopathy, retinal detachments and tears, macular holes, macular puckers, vitreous hemorrhages and traumatic eye injuries as well as other diseases. The retinal surgeon requires a variety of devices and equipment to perform the surgery, such as a vitrectomy machine and vitrector to remove the vitreous from the eye, a light source and endoilluminator to illuminate the eye and a laser and endolaser probe, which provides focused photocoagulation for the treatment of diabetic retinopathy and related conditions.</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 24.5pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Based upon a study performed by Market Scope LLC (&#8220;Market Scope&#8221;), dated March 2012, there are approximately 2,000 practicing retinal specialists in the United States and an additional 7,600 throughout the rest of the world. It is estimated that approximately 327,000 vitrectomies will be performed in the United States and 1.295 million total vitrectomies will be performed throughout the world in 2014.&#160; Market Scope estimates that these procedures are growing 2.4 percent annually.</div>

<div style="MARGIN-TOP: 10pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 10pt; CLEAR: both" id="DSPFPageBreakArea">
<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: right; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', Times, Serif; FONT-SIZE: 8pt" id="DSPFPageNumberArea">8</div>

<div style="WIDTH: 100%" id="DSPFPageHeader">

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 24.5pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Our business continues to grow and evolve as market conditions change. Due to the changing needs of the retina community, the Company designed an enhanced version of the VersaVIT 2.0<sup style="vertical-align: text-top; line-height: 1; font-size: smaller;">TM</sup> vitrectomy machine and&#160;vitrectomy&#160;packs to provide surgeons with a vitrectomy platform that is efficient, versatile, portable, space-saving, and cost effective.&#160;The Company will continue to focus on market needs and market changes to provide surgeons with products that meet their needs.</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="BACKGROUND-COLOR: #ffffff">
<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Marketing and Sales Force</div>

<div>&#160;</div>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 24.5pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In the United States, we have assembled a direct, dedicated sales organization, consisting of 22 sales representatives, nine field sales management/support persons and eight marketing professionals. In fiscal 2014, we expanded our field application specialists by three and our marketing professionals by one to fully implement our VersaVIT 2.0<sup style="vertical-align: text-top; line-height: 1; font-size: smaller;">TM</sup> launch, and we are also working on additional devices and accessories to complement our VersaVIT 2.0<sup style="vertical-align: text-top; line-height: 1; font-size: smaller;">TM</sup> vitrectomy system.&#160; Our team sells vitreoretinal surgical products directly to end-users at hospitals, ambulatory surgery centers and surgeon offices throughout the country. We offer over 1,000 separate catalogue items in the vitreoretinal surgical market, 640 of which are manufactured by or for Synergetics. Our vitreoretinal products include a vitrectomy system under the VersaVIT 2.0<sup style="vertical-align: text-top; line-height: 1; font-size: smaller;">TM</sup> brand, procedural packs under VersaPACK<sup style="vertical-align: text-top; line-height: 1; font-size: smaller;">TM </sup>and Core Essentials<sup style="vertical-align: text-top; line-height: 1; font-size: smaller;">TM</sup> brands, fiberoptic endoilluminators and endolaser probes, a variety of disposable and reusable devices designed for intraocular manipulation of tissues, illumination equipment under the Photon<sup style="vertical-align: text-top; line-height: 1; font-size: smaller;">TM</sup> brand, laser equipment for the United States market under Ellex&#8217;s Solitaire<sup style="vertical-align: text-top; line-height: 1; font-size: smaller;">TM</sup> brand, Volk&#8217;s line of ophthalmic lenses, Labtician&#8217;s scleral buckles and other miscellaneous products.</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 24.5pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Internationally, we utilize a hybrid sales network comprised of direct and distributor sales. We have distribution agreements with independent representatives to sell and distribute our ophthalmic surgical products. On July 8, 2013, we acquired our United Kingdom distributor, M.I.S.S., which added five international employees.&#160; At July 31, 2014, we had 15 international direct sales and distribution employees and were represented by over 80 non-U.S. distributors and independent sales representatives. Our vitreoretinal surgical products are offered for sale in approximately 50 countries outside the United States. The terms of sale to our non-U.S. distributors and our non-U.S. end-user customers do not differ materially from those to our domestic end-user customers. Selling prices are established based upon each country&#8217;s competitive pricing environment.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 24.5pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Competition in the vitreoretinal market is intense and is expected to increase.&#160; This market is characterized by technological innovation and change.&#160; We compete by providing products and services that are valued by our customers such as:&#160; sales relationships, product innovations, and responses to changing market/business needs.&#160; See Item 1A. &#8220;Risk Factors.&#8221;</div>

In addition, our products compete with smaller and larger specialized companies that do not otherwise focus on ophthalmic and vitreoretinal surgery.</div>

On April 2, 2009, the Company executed a new, three-year distribution agreement (effective January 1, 2009) with Codman for the continued distribution by Codman of the fourth generation electrosurgical generator, certain other electrosurgery generators, related disposables and accessories. In addition, the Company entered into a three-year license agreement, which provides for the continued licensing of the Company&#8217;s Malis<sup style="vertical-align: text-top; line-height: 1; font-size: smaller;">&#174;</sup> trademark to Codman for use with certain Codman products, including those covered by the distribution agreement.&#160;In December 2010, Codman elected to exercise its option of exclusive distribution with respect to the electrosurgical generators and related disposables and accessories in the fields of neurocranial and neurospinal surgery. The agreement expires on December 31, 2014.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 24.5pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">On November 16, 2009, the Company announced the signing of an addendum to its three-year agreement with Codman. Under the terms of the revised agreement, Codman has the exclusive right to market and distribute the Company&#8217;s Spetzler<sup style="vertical-align: text-top; line-height: 1; font-size: smaller;">TM</sup>-Malis<sup style="vertical-align: text-top; line-height: 1; font-size: smaller;">&#174;</sup> branded disposable bipolar forceps produced by Synergetics. Codman began distribution of the disposable bipolar forceps in 2009, domestically, and in 2010, internationally.</div>

</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 24.5pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Codman relationship has been proceeding well and is meeting the Company&#8217;s expectations for unit and dollar sales volumes. Sales to Codman in the fiscal year ended July 31, 2014 comprised 23.4 percent of the Company&#8217;s net sales.</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 24.5pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Company supplies a multi-channel ablation generator used for minimally invasive pain control treatment to Stryker pursuant to a supply and distribution agreement dated as of October 25, 2004, as amended.&#160; The agreement expires on June 30, 2015.&#160; The agreement covers the manufacture and supply of the multi-channel ablation generator unit together with certain accessories. The pain control generator can be utilized for facet denervation, rhizotomy, percutaneous cordotomy, dorsal root entry zone lesions, peripheral neuralgia, trigeminal neuralgia and ramus communications. Pain relief is achieved by the controlled heating of the area surrounding the electrode tip. A thermosensor in the probe is used to control tissue temperature. Impedance values are displayed for the user to guard against unsafe conditions. The system provides an electrical stimulator for nerve localization and various coagulating outputs that are selectable based on the procedures undertaken. The pain control generator is designed to produce a bipolar output to minimize current spread, although it can be operated in a monopolar mode as well. The agreement also provides Stryker the right of first refusal for the distribution of other products for use in the field of percutaneous treatment of pain or for use in other fields in conjunction with a generator product having the same features and technical specifications as the products distributed under this agreement.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 24.5pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">On March 31, 2010, the Company entered into a supply agreement with Stryker pursuant to which the Company agreed to supply Stryker with disposable ultrasonic aspirator instrument tips and certain other consumable products used in conjunction with Stryker&#8217;s ultrasonic aspirator console and handpieces.&#160; The agreement expires on March 31, 2016.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 24.5pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Stryker relationship has been proceeding well and is meeting the Company&#8217;s expectations for unit and dollar sales volumes. Sales to Stryker in the fiscal year ended July 31, 2014 comprised 16.6 percent of the Company&#8217;s net sales.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Neurosurgical procedures on a global basis continue to rise at an estimated 1 to 3 percent growth rate driven by an aging global population, new technologies, advances in surgical techniques and a growing global market resulting from ongoing improvements in healthcare delivery in emerging markets, among other factors. Based significantly upon this growth in procedures, sales of neurosurgical products worldwide are forecasted to increase by approximately 4 percent.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Competition</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 24.5pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In the field of neurosurgery, we design, develop and manufacture precision-engineered, surgical devices and instruments. We believe we are the premier manufacturer of bipolar electrosurgical systems for use in neurosurgery. Our neurosurgical bipolar electrosurgical systems and accessories, which are sold by Codman, compete against similar products sold by the Valleylab division of Covidien Ltd., Kirwan Surgical Products, Inc., Erbe Elektromedizin GmbH and the Aesculap division of B. Braun Medical Inc. The ultrasonic aspiration tips and accessories we supply to Stryker compete against similar products sold by Integra Life Sciences Holdings, Corp., the manufacturer of the CUSA<sup style="vertical-align: text-top; line-height: 1; font-size: smaller;">TM</sup> and the Selector<sup style="vertical-align: text-top; line-height: 1; font-size: smaller;">TM</sup> ultrasonic aspirator systems, and Misonix, Inc.&#160; Additionally, the products we manufacture compete with smaller and larger specialized companies. These products also compete with other technologies, such as handheld instruments and a variety of tissue removal systems designed for removing skull-based tumors.&#160; See Item 1A. &#8220;Risk Factors.&#8221;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Operations</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Manufacturing and Supplies</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">We design, manufacture and assemble the majority of our ophthalmic, direct neurosurgical and certain of our OEM products in our facility in O&#8217;Fallon, Missouri.&#160; The bipolar electrosurgical generators (including the neurosurgical, pain control and other generator units) are manufactured in our facility in King of Prussia, Pennsylvania.&#160; We are in process of transitioning this manufacturing to O&#8217;Fallon, Missouri which we believe will be completed by mid-fiscal 2015.&#160; The Solitaire<sup style="vertical-align: text-top; line-height: 1; font-size: smaller;">TM</sup> laser and the Volk lenses are purchased by the Company from their respective manufacturers.&#160; Our products are assembled from raw materials and components supplied to us by third parties.&#160; Most of the raw materials and components we use in the manufacture of our products are available from more than one supplier.&#160; For some components, there are relatively few alternate sources of supply.&#160; For a portion of our disposable product line and for several key components of our Photon<sup style="vertical-align: text-top; line-height: 1; font-size: smaller;">TM</sup> light sources, our VersaVIT 2.0<sup style="vertical-align: text-top; line-height: 1; font-size: smaller;">TM</sup> vitrectomy system and our electrosurgical generators, we rely upon single source suppliers or contract manufacturers.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">During the fiscal year ended July 31, 2014, we continued our&#160;improvement&#160;journey and have introduced all of our manufacturing lines to&#160;a lean methodology.&#160; These manufacturing lines are at varying degrees of maturity with respect to implementing the continuous improvement&#160;&#160;methodology.&#160; In fiscal 2015, we expect to continue the maturation process.&#160; Throughout the year, we have been able to increase our sales by 2.2 percent without any significant increase in the manufacturing footprint.</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Government Regulations</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Medical devices manufactured by the Company are subject to extensive regulation by governmental authorities, including federal, state and non-U.S. governmental agencies.&#160; The principal regulator in the United States is the FDA.&#160; The medical device regulatory scheme in the European Union is driven by the Medical Device Directive.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">FDA regulations are wide-ranging and govern the development, production and marketing of medical devices, the observance of certain standards with respect to the design, manufacture, testing, labeling and promotion of devices, the maintenance and retention of certain records, the ability to track devices in distribution, the reporting of potential product defects and patient incidents, the export of devices and other matters.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">All medical devices introduced into the market since May 28, 1976, which include all of our products, are required by the FDA as a condition of sale and marketing to secure either a 510(k) Premarket Notification clearance or an approved Premarket Approval Application (&#8220;PMA&#8221;) unless specifically exempted by regulation.&#160; A Premarket Notification clearance indicates FDA agreement with an applicant&#8217;s determination that the product for which clearance has been sought is substantially equivalent to another medical device that was on the market before 1976 or that has received 510(k) Premarket Notification clearance since that time.&#160; The process of obtaining a Premarket Notification clearance can take several months or potentially years and may require the submission of limited clinical data and supporting information.&#160; The PMA process typically requires the submission of significant quantities of clinical data and manufacturing information and involves significant review costs.&#160; The Company does not anticipate any of our new devices in development at this time will require a PMA.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Under FDA regulations, after a device receives 510(k) clearance, any modification that could significantly affect its safety or effectiveness, or that would constitute a major change in the intended use of the device, technology, materials or packaging, requires a new 510(k) clearance.&#160; The FDA requires a manufacturer to make this determination in the first instance, but the FDA can review any such decision.&#160;&#160; If the FDA disagrees, it can require a manufacturer to obtain a new 510(k) clearance or it can seek enforcement action against the manufacturer.</div>

<div style="MARGIN-TOP: 10pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 10pt; CLEAR: both" id="DSPFPageBreakArea">
<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: right; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', Times, Serif; FONT-SIZE: 8pt" id="DSPFPageNumberArea">11</div>

<hr style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: always; BORDER-RIGHT-WIDTH: 0px; BACKGROUND-COLOR: #000000; MARGIN: 4px 0px; WIDTH: 100%; BORDER-TOP-WIDTH: 0px; BORDER-BOTTOM-WIDTH: 0px; HEIGHT: 2px; COLOR: #000000; CLEAR: both; BORDER-LEFT-WIDTH: 0px" id="DSPFPageBreak" noshade="noshade">
<div style="WIDTH: 100%" id="DSPFPageHeader">
<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 8pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal"><a href="#TABLEOFCONTENTS">Table of Contents</a></div>
</div>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">We are also required to register with the FDA as a device manufacturer and to maintain compliance with the FDA&#8217;s Quality System Regulations (&#8220;QSR&#8221;).&#160; The QSR incorporates the requirements of Good Manufacturing Practice as well as other regulatory requirements of the FDA, which mandate detailed quality assurance and record-keeping procedures and subject manufacturers to unscheduled periodic quality system inspections.&#160; We conduct internal quality assurance audits to ensure compliance throughout the manufacturing process.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">We may not promote or advertise our products for uses not within the scope of our clearances or approvals or make unsupported safety or effectiveness claims.&#160; Further, we are required to comply with various FDA regulations for labeling and promotion.&#160; The Medical Device Reporting regulations require that we provide information to the FDA whenever there is evidence to reasonably suggest that one of our devices may have caused or contributed to a death or serious injury.&#160; In addition, the FDA prohibits us from promoting a medical device before marketing clearance has been received or promoting a cleared device for unapproved indications. Noncompliance with applicable regulatory requirements can result in enforcement action, which is more fully described in Part 1, Item 1A, &#8220;Risk Factors&#8221; section of this Annual Report on Form 10-K.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Medical device regulations also are in effect in many of the countries outside the United States in which our products are sold.&#160; These laws range from comprehensive device approval and quality system requirements for some or all of our medical device products to simpler requests for product data or certifications.&#160; The number and scope of these requirements are increasing.&#160; In June 1998, the European Union Medical Device Directives became effective, and all medical devices sold in the European common market must meet the Medical Device Directives standards. The Company sells its products in the European medical device market; as such, we have voluntarily chosen to participate in audits established by the European Union through which we have obtained &#8220;CE marking&#8221; for many of our products.&#160; The Company is subjected to annual audits at both of our manufacturing facilities for compliance to the quality system standards established by the International Standards Organization (&#8220;ISO&#8221;) and Medical Device Directives established by European law.&#160; The Company is certified to ISO 13485:2003, the international standard for quality systems as applied to medical devices.&#160; Failure to correct deficiencies discovered during an audit could result in the removal of the CE mark on our products, which would effectively bar the sale of the Company&#8217;s products in the European market.&#160; Such a result would have a significant and material negative impact on the Company and its business.&#160; In addition, there are several&#160;countries&#160;outside the European Union&#160;which&#160;require additional complex regulatory clearances.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Management believes that we are in material compliance with the government regulations governing our business in the countries where we market our products.</div>

<div>&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Safety Approvals</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The majority of our capital equipment products also require electrical safety testing, and in some cases electromagnetic emission testing, either as a product registration requirement and/or to gain market acceptance.&#160; Testing to internationally recognized standards is provided by third party vendors, who certify our products&#8217; compliance to these standards.&#160; The primary standard to which our capital equipment must comply requires that we provide detailed risk management documentation to support the electrical safety testing.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Intellectual Property</div>

<div>&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt">Our continuing technological innovations and superior engineering designs, as well as the goodwill associated with our products, provide us with competitive advantages, many of which are proprietary to the Company.&#160; We protect our proprietary advantages, in large part, by obtaining legal rights in issued patents, the filing of patent applications, maintaining trade secrets and confidential know how, and through the use of trademarks.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt">Patented and/or patent pending technology is used in most of our product lines, from our most recently released surgical equipment, the VersaVIT 2.0<sup style="vertical-align: text-top; line-height: 1; font-size: smaller;">TM</sup> vitrectomy system and its associated disposables, to our line of Directional Laser Probe<sup style="vertical-align: text-top; line-height: 1; font-size: smaller;">TM</sup> devices, our DDMS<sup style="vertical-align: text-top; line-height: 1; font-size: smaller;">TM</sup> membrane scrapers, our Photon<sup style="vertical-align: text-top; line-height: 1; font-size: smaller;">TM</sup> line of illumination technology with complimentary accessories, and further, to the products we make for our OEM partners, such as our Malis<sup style="vertical-align: text-top; line-height: 1; font-size: smaller;">&#174;</sup> line of bipolar electrosurgical generators, forceps and other accessories, as well as certain surgical ultrasonic aspiration tips.&#160; When deemed appropriate for our business success, we have chosen to and will continue to choose to enforce and defend these patent rights.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">We generally seek patent protection on those technological advancements that are believed to be patentable and are planned or likely to be used in our products or product improvements.&#160; Currently, the Company owns 114 unexpired patents around the world, 40 of which have been issued in the United States.&#160; Our oldest, unexpired patent was issued in the United States about 16 years ago, in 1998.&#160; Given the range of ages of the patents in our portfolio, we expect that patent expiration will be a routine event going forward for some time.&#160; We do not believe that the expiration of any one patent, or the expiration over time of each of our currently unexpired patents, will have a material, adverse effect on our business.&#160; Furthermore, we manage our patent portfolio such that we will purge a patent application or an issued patent from our portfolio when we determine that the offensive and defensive value of such patent or application is outweighed by its costs of maintenance.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Through our research and development efforts, we are continually creating new intellectual property, and continue to file patent applications around the world to protect our rights in these developments.&#160; The Company has numerous, pending patent applications in the United States and in other countries.&#160; We believe that these patent applications will mature into issued patents in due course; however, we also know that other legal rights, whether of other inventors or of the public, ultimately may prevent our applications from issuing as patents.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">We do not rely exclusively on our patents to provide us with intellectual property protections, but we also rely on trade secrets, know-how, and trademarks.&#160; In an effort to protect our trade secrets and know-how, we generally require our employees, consultants, and advisors to enter into confidentiality agreements with us upon the commencement of their respective relationships with us.&#160; These confidentiality agreements typically provide that all confidential information developed or disclosed by us during the course of the relationship must be kept confidential and cannot be used except to further the purposes of the relationship.&#160; To the extent that such confidential information is likely to include inventions, our agreements with our employees, consultants, and advisors may also contain provisions requiring these individuals to assign to us any inventions conceived or reduced to practice in the course of the relationship.</div>

Stroisch joined the Company in the Engineering division in September 1995.&#160; In his 19 years with the Company, Mr. Stroisch has had increasing levels of responsibility within the organization, including International Product Manager, International Sales Manager and Vice President of Ophthalmic Sales.&#160; In April 2009, he was promoted to Vice President of International Sales and Marketing.&#160; In August 2012, oversight of our R&amp;D efforts was added to his responsibilities and he became Vice President of Marketing and Technology.&#160; Mr. Stroisch coordinates and supervises the marketing efforts of the Company and the scientific development of the Company&#8217;s products.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Our competitive position depends on multiple, complex factors, including our ability to achieve market acceptance for our products, develop new products, implement production and marketing plans, secure regulatory approvals for products under development and protect our intellectual property.&#160; We may need to develop new applications for our products to remain competitive.&#160; Technological advances outside of our field, such as in pharmacology, by one or more of our current or future competitors could render our present or future products obsolete or uneconomical.&#160; Our future success depends, among other things, upon our ability to compete effectively against current technology, as well as to respond effectively to technological advances, and upon our ability to successfully implement our marketing strategies and execute our R&amp;D plan.</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In addition, our VersaVIT 2.0<sup style="vertical-align: text-top; line-height: 1; font-size: smaller;">TM</sup> is complex in design and the manufacturing involves a highly complex and precise process.&#160; As a result of the technical complexity, changes in our or our suppliers&#8217; manufacturing processes or the inadvertent use of defective materials by us or our suppliers could result in a material adverse effect on our ability to achieve acceptable manufacturing yields and product reliability.&#160; To the extent that we do not achieve such yields or product reliability, our business, operating results, financial condition and customer relationships would be adversely affected.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">New products and enhancements usually require a substantial investment in R&amp;D before we can determine the viability of the product.&#160; We currently have 24 active projects in the development pipeline. We spent approximately 8.0 percent of our sales on R&amp;D during the fiscal year ended July 31, 2014, and we expect to spend 6 to 8 percent of our sales for this purpose in future periods.&#160; Our R&amp;D process entails considerable uncertainty.&#160; Moreover, new products and enhancements may not produce revenues in excess of the R&amp;D costs, and they may become obsolete by changing customer preferences or the introduction by our competitors of new technologies or features.&#160; Failure to develop our manufacturing capability may mean that even if we develop promising new products, we may not be able to produce them profitably, as a result of delays and additional capital investment costs.&#160; Any failure in our ability to successfully develop and introduce new products or enhanced versions of existing products could have a material adverse effect on our operating results and would cause our net revenues to decline.</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">A significant part of our product sales comes from two customers, which makes us vulnerable to the loss of those customers.</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">During the fiscal year ended July 31, 2014, revenue from sales of our bipolar electrosurgical generators, disposable bipolar forceps, cord tubing sets and royalty payments from Codman represented approximately 23.4 percent of the Company&#8217;s total net sales.&#160; Under our existing agreement with Codman, it distributes all contract products on an exclusive basis and has exclusive rights to distribute all monopolar and bipolar generators for use in neurocranial and neurospinal surgery.&#160; The initial term of our existing agreement with Codman expired on December 31, 2011, after which the agreement entered into a single, automatic, three-year renewal term.&#160; The agreement expires on December 31, 2014.&#160; We continue to enhance the contract products and to develop new additions to the disposable bipolar forceps line for Codman which we expect will expand their reach to additional markets.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In addition, revenue from the sales of our pain control generators, the ultrasonic aspirator tips and accessories sold by Stryker accounted for 16.6 percent of the Company&#8217;s total net sales for fiscal 2014.&#160; Under our existing agreements with Stryker, it distributes the pain control generator and ultrasonic aspirator tips on an exclusive basis.&#160; The pain control generator agreement expires on June 30, 2015, and the ultrasonic aspirator tip agreement expires on March 31, 2016.&#160; We continue to develop new ultrasonic aspirator tips with Stryker which we expect will expand their reach to additional markets.</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Our King of Prussia closure plan exposes us to risk, and we may not realize the expected benefits.</div>

<div>&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt">Transferring manufacturing of medical devices is more expensive, time-consuming and riskier than similar transfers in less regulated industries.&#160; Regulatory approval to sell our products is generally limited to the current manufacturing site, and changing the site requires the approval from regulatory bodies and our OEM partners prior to commercialization.&#160; To satisfy our own quality standards as well as comply with applicable regulations, we must follow strict protocols to confirm that products made at a new site are equivalent to those made at the currently approved site.&#160; Even minor changes in equipment, supplies or processes require validation.&#160; While we have placed a priority on maintaining the continuity and quality of product supply, including increasing our inventory as safety stock during the closure, unanticipated delays or difficulties in the transfer process could interrupt our supply of products.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt">In fiscal&#160;2014, we have expended $682,000 on the closure plan.&#160; The goal of the project is to increase our operating margins by $1.1 million on an annualized basis beginning in fiscal 2016.&#160; We cannot assure that we will achieve the expected benefits of this initiative.</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Our international operations subject us to certain operating risks, which could adversely impact our net sales, results of operations and financial condition.</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Sales of our products outside the U.S. represented approximately 25 percent of our revenue in 2014.&#160;Many of the products we sell to our OEM customers in the U.S. are subsequently shipped to their non-U.S. customers in various countries around the world, but revenue attributable to these sales is included in our domestic revenues. As of July 31, 2014, we sell our ophthalmic products outside the U.S. through five direct sales organizations in Australia, France, Germany, Italy and the United Kingdom, after our acquisition of M.I.S.S. on July 8, 2013.&#160; The results of operations and the financial position of certain of our foreign operations are reported in the relevant local currencies and then translated into U.S. dollars at the applicable exchange rates for inclusion in our consolidated financial statements, exposing us to translation risk.&#160; Our most significant currency exposures are to the Great Britain Pound (&#8220;GBP&#8221;) and the euro.&#160; The exchange rates between the GBP and the euro in comparison to the U.S. dollar may fluctuate substantially.&#160; We have not attempted to offset our exposure to these risks by investing in derivatives or engaging in hedging activities.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">We may face manufacturing and quality control challenges which could impact our competitive advantage.</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The manufacturing of our surgical equipment and disposable accessories is a highly complex and precise process.&#160; We assemble critical components and sub-assemblies and substantially all our final products at our facilities in O&#8217;Fallon, Missouri and King of Prussia, Pennsylvania. We are in process of transitioning this manufacturing to O&#8217;Fallon, Missouri which we believe will be completed by mid-fiscal 2015.&#160; We may experience manufacturing difficulties, quality control issues or manufacturing constraints, particularly with regards to new products and increased production demands.&#160; If our sales increase substantially, we may need to increase our production and quality control capacity and may not be able to do so in a timely, effective or cost efficient manner.&#160; We may not be able to manufacture sufficient quantities of our products which may require us to qualify other manufacturers of our products.&#160; Furthermore, we may experience delays, disruptions, capacity constraints or quality control problems in our manufacturing operations and as a result, product shipments to our customers could be delayed, which would negatively impact our net sales.&#160; Also, we may overestimate the demand for our product leading to excess inventory, which would increase our inventory carrying costs and increase the risk of inventory write-downs.&#160; Any of these occurrences would negatively impact our business and operating results.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In addition, quality is extremely important to us and our customers due to the serious and costly consequences of product failure.&#160; Our quality certifications are critical to the marketing success of our products.&#160; If we fail to meet these standards, our reputation could be damaged, we could lose customers and our revenue and results of operations could decline.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">If any of our single source or limited source suppliers were to cease providing components, we</font>&#160;<font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">may not be able to produce certain products.</font></div>

<div>&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt">Our products are assembled from raw materials and components supplied to us by third parties.&#160; Most of the raw materials and components used in the manufacturing of our products are available from more than one supplier.&#160; For some components, there are relatively few alternate sources of supply.&#160; However, we rely upon single source suppliers or contract manufacturers for a portion of our disposable product lines and for several key components of our Photon<sup style="vertical-align: text-top; line-height: 1; font-size: smaller;">TM</sup> light sources, our VersaVIT 2.0<sup style="vertical-align: text-top; line-height: 1; font-size: smaller;">TM</sup> vitrectomy system and our electrosurgical generators.&#160; In addition, these suppliers must also adhere to the FDA&#8217;s rigorous manufacturing standards.&#160; Our profit margins and our ability to develop and deliver products on a timely basis may be adversely affected by the lack of alternative supply in the required timeframe.</div>

<div>&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt">We may experience decreasing prices for our goods and services due to pricing pressure experienced by our customers from managed care organizations and third-party payers, increased market power of our customers as the medical device industry consolidates and increased competition among medical engineering and manufacturing service providers.&#160; If the prices for our products decrease and we are unable to reduce our expenses, our results of operations will be adversely affected.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Our facilities could be subject to catastrophic loss such as fire, flood, tornados or earthquake. A substantial portion of our R&amp;D and manufacturing activities, our corporate headquarters and other critical business operations are located in O&#8217;Fallon, Missouri and California near major fault lines which could experience an earthquake. We maintain property and business interruption insurance coverage at levels we have determined are reasonable.&#160; Any such loss at any of our facilities could disrupt our operations, delay production, shipments and revenue and result in large expenses to repair and replace our facilities.</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Security breaches and other disruptions could compromise our information and expose us to liability, which would cause our business and reputation to suffer.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In the ordinary course of our business, we collect and store sensitive data, including intellectual property, our proprietary business information and that of our customers, suppliers and business partners, and personally identifiable information of our customers and employees, in our data center and on our networks. The secure processing, maintenance and transmission of this information is critical to our operations. Despite our security measures, our information technology and infrastructure may be vulnerable to attacks by hackers or breached due to employee error, malfeasance or other disruptions. Any such breach could compromise our networks and the information stored there could be accessed, publicly disclosed, lost or stolen. Any such access, disclosure or other loss of information could result in legal claims or proceedings, liability under laws that protect the privacy of personal information, disrupt our operations and harm our reputation, which could adversely affect our business, revenues and competitive position.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Risks related to Our Financial Condition</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">We are subject to credit risk from our accounts receivable related to our product sales, which include sales within European and emerging market countries that are currently experiencing economic turmoil.</div>

<div>&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt">The majority of our accounts receivable arise from product sales in the U.S. Our accounts receivable in the U.S. are primarily due from OEM partners, public and private hospitals and ambulatory surgery centers.&#160; However, we also have receivable balances from customers within the European Union, Turkey, Canada, Japan, Russia and Brazil.&#160; Our accounts receivable outside the U.S. are due from independent distributors and, to a lesser extent, public and private hospitals.&#160; Our historic write-offs of accounts receivable have not been significant.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt">We monitor the financial performance and creditworthiness of our customers so that we can properly assess and respond to changes in their credit profile.&#160; Our independent distributors operate in Spain, Italy and Greece, among other countries, where economic conditions continue to present challenges to our independent distributors&#8217; businesses, and thus, could place at risk the amount due to us from them.</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Our cash maintained with a bank may not be fully insured.</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">We maintain significant amounts of cash and cash equivalents at a financial institution that is in excess of federally insured limits.&#160; Given the current instability of financial institutions, we cannot be assured that we will not experience losses on these deposits.</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">We have significant goodwill and other intangible assets and potential impairment of goodwill and other intangibles may significantly impact our profitability.</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Goodwill and intangible assets represent a significant portion of our total assets.&#160; Finite-lived intangibles assets are subject to an impairment analysis whenever events or changes in circumstances indicate the carrying amount of the asset may not be recoverable.&#160; Goodwill and indefinite-lived intangibles assets are tested annually for impairment if events or changes in circumstances indicate that the asset may be impaired.&#160; If an impairment exists, we would be required to take an impairment charge with respect to the impaired asset.&#160; Events giving rise to impairment are difficult to predict and are an inherent risk in the medical device industry.&#160; As a result of the significance of goodwill and intangible assets, our financial condition and results of operations in a future period could be negatively impacted should such an impairment of goodwill or intangible assets occur.</div>
