<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Risks related to the Regulation of our Industry</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Uncertainty regarding U.S. healthcare reform measures, other healthcare regulatory changes and changes in third-party coverage and reimbursement policies could adversely affect our revenue and financial condition.</div>

<div>&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt">The Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act as modified by the Health Care and Education Reconciliation Act were enacted into law in March 2010.&#160; Certain provisions of the law will not be effective for a number of years, and there are many programs and requirements for which the details have not yet been fully established or consequences not fully understood.&#160; It is unclear what the full impacts will be from the law.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt">The Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act imposes an excise tax on domestic sales of class I, II and III medical devices at the rate of 2.3 percent of sales revenue, for which medical device manufacturers became liable beginning in January 2013.&#160; Substantially all of our products are class I and II medical devices.&#160; The inability to offset this tax could have a material impact on results of operations.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt">The law also focuses on a number of Medicare provisions aimed at improving quality and decreasing costs, though we are not certain of the impact that these provisions will have on patient access to new technologies and medical procedures.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt">Additional changes in government legislation or regulation, or changes in private third-party payers&#8217; policies toward reimbursement for procedures employing our products, may prohibit adequate reimbursement.&#160; There have been a number of legislative and regulatory proposals to change the healthcare system, reduce the cost of healthcare and change medical reimbursement policies.&#160; Further proposed legislation or regulation and policy changes affecting third-party reimbursement are likely.&#160; We cannot predict what legislation or regulation, if any, relating to the health care industry or third-party coverage and reimbursement may be enacted in the future, or what the effect of such legislation or regulation may have on us.&#160; However, any changes that lower reimbursement for our products or reduce medical procedure volumes could adversely affect our business and results of operations.</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Our industry is experiencing greater scrutiny and regulation by governmental authorities, which may lead to greater governmental regulation in the future.</div>

<div>&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt">Medical device companies are subject to rigorous regulation, including by the FDA and numerous other federal, state and foreign governmental authorities.&#160; These authorities and members of the United States Congress have been increasing their scrutiny of our industry.&#160; In addition, certain states have recently passed or are considering legislation restricting our interactions with health care providers and requiring disclosure of payments to them.&#160; As a result, the Physician Payment Sunshine Act enacted in 2010 imposes reporting and disclosure requirements on device and drug manufacturers for any &#8220;transfers of value&#8221; made or distributed to health care providers licensed by certain states and, starting with payments or other transfers of value made on or after August 1, 2013, to all U.S. physicians and U.S. teaching hospitals at the federal level.&#160; Failure to submit this required information may result in significant civil monetary penalties.&#160; While we have developed corporate compliance programs based on what we believe to be current best practices, we cannot assure you that we or our employees or agents are or will be in compliance with all applicable federal, state or foreign regulations and laws.&#160; We anticipate that the various governments will continue to closely scrutinize our industry, and additional regulations by governmental authorities may increase compliance costs, exposure to litigation and other adverse effects to our operations.</div>

<div><br>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Delays in the receipt of or our failure to receive regulatory clearances or approvals, the loss of previously received clearances or approvals, or failure to comply with existing or future regulatory requirements could have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition, results of operations and future growth prospects.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Our R&amp;D activities and the manufacturing, labeling, distribution and marketing of our existing and future products are subject to regulation by governmental agencies in the United States and in other countries.&#160; The FDA and comparable agencies in other countries impose mandatory procedures and standards for the conduct of clinical trials and the production and marketing of products for medical diagnostic and therapeutic use.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Products under development are subject to FDA approval or clearance prior to commercial use.&#160; The process of obtaining necessary FDA approvals or clearances is not only costly, but can potentially take years and the outcome may be uncertain.&#160; Our inability to obtain required regulatory approval or clearance in a timely manner could harm our business.&#160; Further, approval or clearance may place substantial restrictions on the indications for which the product may be marketed or to whom it may be marketed.&#160; Additional studies may be required to gain approval or clearance for the use of a product for clinical indications other than those for which the product was initially approved or cleared or for changes to the product.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Furthermore, an additional risk relates to the regulatory classification of new products or proposed new uses for existing products.&#160; With each application, we are required to make a judgment about the appropriate form and content of the application.&#160; If the FDA disagrees with our judgment in any particular case and, for example, requires us to file a premarket approval application rather than a Section 510(k) premarket notification or requires clinical data be added to our application, the time and expense required to obtain the approval might be significantly increased and approval may become less likely.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Once approved or cleared for marketing, our products are subject to continuing FDA requirements, such as those relating to quality control and quality assurance, maintenance of records, reporting of adverse events and product recalls, documentation and labeling and restrictions on promotion of medical devices.&#160; Failure to precisely follow any of these requirements may lead to unanticipated costs of remediation, a product recall and/or an order to cease production and sales of a product. </font>A recall could divert management&#8217;s attention, cause us to incur significant expenses, harm our reputation with customers and negatively affect our future net sales.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">There can be no assurance that we will be able to obtain necessary clearances or approvals to market any new products, or to market existing products for new intended uses, on a timely basis, if at all.&#160; There can be no assurance that we will be able to continue to market existing products without interruption due to regulatory oversight.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Moreover, for the majority of our non-direct, foreign sales, our distributors assist with and control regulatory approval or clearance for product marketing.&#160; We cannot be certain that such approvals or clearances are actually effective.&#160; Nor can we be assured that approval or clearance for product marketing in any given country would continue to be effective for any distributor other than our current distributor in that same country, if any of our current distributors cease to distribute our products.&#160; A change in our distributor in any country could lead to delays in continued sales in that country while regulatory approval or clearances are sought to be renewed.&#160; Such a delay could have significant impacts on our net sales outside the U.S.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">We may be subject to penalties and may be precluded from marketing</font>&#160;<font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">our products if we fail to comply with extensive governmental regulations.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Changes in tax laws or exposure to additional income tax liabilities could have a material impact on our financial condition and results of operations.</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">We are subject to income taxes as well as non-income based taxes, in both the U.S. and various jurisdictions outside the U.S.&#160; We are subject to ongoing tax audits in various jurisdictions.&#160; Tax authorities may disagree with certain positions we have taken and assess additional taxes and penalties.&#160; We regularly assess the likely outcomes of these audits in order to determine the appropriateness of our tax provision.&#160; However, there can be no assurance that we will accurately predict the outcomes of these audits, and the actual outcomes of these audits could have a material impact on our consolidated earnings and financial condition.&#160; Additionally, changes in tax laws or tax rulings could materially impact our effective tax rate. For example, recent legislation imposed on medical device manufacturers a 2.3 percent excise tax on U.S. sales of medical devices beginning in January 2013. Proposals for fundamental U.S. corporate tax reform, if enacted, could have a material impact on our future results of operations.</div>

<div><br>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Our intellectual property rights may not provide meaningful commercial protection</font>&#160;<font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">for our products, which could adversely affect our ability to compete in the</font>&#160;<font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">market.</font></div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Our ability to compete effectively depends, in part, on our ability to maintain the proprietary nature of our technologies and manufacturing processes, which includes the ability to obtain, protect and enforce patents on our technology and to protect our trade secrets.&#160; We own patents that cover significant aspects of our products.&#160; Certain patents of ours have expired and others will expire in the future.&#160; Competitors may develop products similar to ours that our patents do not cover.&#160; In addition, our current and future patent applications may not result in the issuance of patents in the United States or other countries.&#160; Further, there is a substantial backlog of patent applications in the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office and the approval or rejection of patent applications may take several years.&#160; In addition, challenges may be made to our patents in the courts or any of various patent offices around the world, and as a result our patents could be narrowed, invalidated or rendered unenforceable.&#160; We may incur substantial costs and resources in applying for and prosecuting these patent, trademark and other intellectual property rights.</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Our competitive position depends, in part, upon unpatented trade secrets, which can be difficult to protect. Others may independently develop substantially equivalent proprietary information and techniques or gain access to our trade secrets.&#160; In an effort to protect our trade secrets, we require consultants, advisors and most of our employees to execute confidentiality agreements and certain of them to sign invention assignment agreements upon commencement of employment or a consulting relationship with us.&#160; Some jurisdictions limit the enforceability and scope of these agreements, and these agreements may not provide meaningful protection for our trade secrets or other proprietary information in the event of the unauthorized use or disclosure of confidential information.</div>

<div><br>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In addition, the laws of certain countries in which we market some of our products do not protect our intellectual property rights to the same extent as the laws of the U.S.&#160; If we are unable to protect our intellectual property in these countries, it could have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition or results of operations.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">The intellectual property rights of others may adversely affect our ability to introduce new products or continue to sell existing products.</div>

<div><br>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The medical device industry is characterized by frequent litigation regarding patent and other intellectual property rights.&#160; Companies in the medical device industry have employed intellectual property litigation to gain a competitive advantage.&#160; Numerous patents are held by others, including academic institutions and our competitors.&#160; These patents may be employed to limit our ability to market our products, for example, through patent infringement litigation.&#160; Patent applications generally will be published 18 months after the filing date.&#160; However, since patent applications continue to be maintained in secrecy for at least some period of time, we cannot assure you that our technology does not infringe any patents, patent applications held by third parties, prior patents, or prior art.&#160; We have, from time to time, been notified of, or have otherwise been made aware of, claims that we are infringing upon patents or other proprietary intellectual property owned by others.&#160; If it appears necessary or desirable, we may seek licenses under such patents or proprietary intellectual property.&#160; Although patent holders may offer such licenses, licenses under such patents or intellectual property may not be offered or the terms of any offered licenses may not be reasonable.&#160; Any infringement claims, with or without merit, and regardless of whether we are successful on the merits, could be time-consuming, result in costly litigation and diversion of technical and management personnel, cause shipment delays or require us to develop non-infringing technology or enter into royalty or licensing agreements.&#160; An adverse determination could prevent us from manufacturing or selling our products, which could have a material adverse effect on our business, results of operations and financial condition.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt">In addition, our common stock may experience an imbalance between supply and demand resulting from low trading volumes, and therefore broad market fluctuations could have a significant impact on the market price of our common stock regardless of our performance.</div>

<div><br>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Synergetics USA, Inc. has anti-takeover defenses that could delay or prevent an</font>&#160;<font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">acquisition and could adversely affect the price of its common stock.</font></div>

<div>&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt">Provisions of our certificate of incorporation, bylaws and Delaware law may have the effect of deterring hostile takeovers or delaying or preventing changes in the control of the Company, including transactions in which our shareholders might otherwise receive a premium for their shares over then current market prices.&#160; In addition, these provisions may limit the ability of our shareholders to approve transactions that they may deem to be in their best interest.&#160; Also, our Board of Directors is divided into three classes, as nearly equal in size as practicable, with three-year staggered terms.&#160; This provision may deter a potential acquirer from engaging in a transaction with us because it will be unable to gain control of our Board of Directors until at least two annual meetings have been held in which directors are elected by our shareholders.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Because we do not intend to pay dividends, stockholders will benefit from an investment in our common stock only if it appreciates in value.</div>

<div>&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt">We have not paid any dividends on our common stock since inception.&#160; We currently expect to retain any earnings for use to further develop our business, and we do not expect to declare cash dividends on our common stock in the foreseeable future.&#160; The declaration and payment of any such dividends in the future depends upon our earnings, financial condition, capital needs and other factors deemed relevant by our Board of Directors, and may be restricted by agreements with lenders.&#160; As a result, the success of an investment in our common stock will depend entirely upon future appreciation.&#160; There is no guarantee that our common stock will appreciate in value or even maintain the price at which stockholders have purchased their shares.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Our primary office and manufacturing operations are conducted in a 60,000 square foot building owned by Synergetics&#8217; wholly owned subsidiary, Synergetics Development Company, LLC, a Missouri limited liability company.&#160; The facility is located in O&#8217;Fallon, Missouri, approximately 25 miles west of St. Louis, Missouri.&#160; We also lease 19,200 square feet of additional space adjacent to our headquarters in O&#8217;Fallon, Missouri, pursuant to a lease that expires on February 29, 2016.&#160; The additional space houses the advanced technology and engineering group as well as the manufacturing and servicing of our capital equipment.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">We also lease 13,500 square feet of space in King of Prussia, Pennsylvania, which is used for office, engineering, and OEM manufacturing activities.&#160; The lease for this facility expires on October 31, 2015.&#160; The closure of the King of Prussia facility is expected to occur by December 31, 2014.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Our subsidiary, M.I.S.S., owns a 1,703 square foot building located approximately 90 kilometers outside of London which serves as office and warehouse space for our United Kingdom operations.&#160; We also lease 746 square feet next to the owned facility, which is used as our European warehouse.&#160; The lease expires on November 30, 2015.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In addition, we lease a 13,000 square foot building in California which is used for office, OEM manufacturing and distribution activities.&#160; The lease expires on November 30, 2017.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">We believe that these facilities are suitable and adequate for our current operations.&#160; Given our continuous improvement initiatives, we believe that we have the ability to generate additional production capacity using our existing manufacturing facilities.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Our Business</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Company is a medical device company. Through continuous improvement and development of our people, our <font style="FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">mission</font> is to design, manufacture and market innovative surgical devices, surgical equipment and consumables of the highest quality in order to assist and enable surgeons who perform surgery around the world to provide a better quality of life for their patients. The Company&#8217;s primary focus is on the surgical disciplines of ophthalmology (vitreoretinal) and neurosurgery. Our distribution channels include a combination of direct and independent sales organizations and important strategic alliances with market leaders. The Company&#8217;s product lines focus upon precision engineered disposable and reusable devices, surgical equipment, procedural kits and the delivery of laser energy, ultrasound, electrosurgery, aspiration, illumination and irrigation, often delivered in multiple combinations. Enterprise-wide sales information is included in Note 17 to the consolidated audited financial statements.</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="MARGIN-TOP: 10pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 10pt; CLEAR: both" id="DSPFPageBreakArea">
<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: right; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', Times, Serif; FONT-SIZE: 8pt" id="DSPFPageNumberArea">30</div>

<hr style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: always; BORDER-RIGHT-WIDTH: 0px; BACKGROUND-COLOR: #000000; MARGIN: 4px 0px; WIDTH: 100%; BORDER-TOP-WIDTH: 0px; BORDER-BOTTOM-WIDTH: 0px; HEIGHT: 2px; COLOR: #000000; CLEAR: both; BORDER-LEFT-WIDTH: 0px" id="DSPFPageBreak" noshade="noshade">
<div style="WIDTH: 100%" id="DSPFPageHeader">
<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 8pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal"><a href="#TABLEOFCONTENTS">Table of Contents</a></div>
</div>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Demand Trends</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 24.5pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Company&#8217;s sales increased 3.1 percent during the fiscal year ended July 31, 2014 (including $1.3 million of deferred revenue recognized) compared with the previous fiscal year.&#160; The most significant factor impacting this increase was a $2.2 million increase in OEM sales.&#160; The increased OEM sales were partially offset by a $0.2 million decrease in ophthalmic sales. Currently, disposable product sales account for approximately 86.9 percent of our total product sales.&#160; Overall sales of our disposable products grew $5.3 million, or 10.2 percent, in fiscal 2014 as compared to fiscal 2013. Sales of capital equipment decreased by approximately $3.2 million, or 30.9 percent, in fiscal 2014 as compared to fiscal 2013 due to macroeconomic condition constraints.</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 24.5pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">A study performed by Market Scope in March 2012 predicts a steady growth of 2.4 percent per year in retinal procedures worldwide driven by an increase in emerging market demand, an increase in the worldwide elderly population, an increase in the number of surgeons, an increase in the number of diseases treated with vitrectomy and an increase in frequency of diabetic complications due to the obesity epidemic.&#160; Based upon this growth in procedures, sales of ophthalmology products worldwide are forecasted to increase by approximately 5.5%.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 24.5pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Neurosurgical procedures on a gl<font style="FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">obal basis continue to rise at an estimated 1 to 3 percent growth rate driven by an aging global population, new technologies, advances in surgical techniques and a growing global market resulting from ongoing improvements in healthcare delivery in emerging market countries, among other factors. Based upon this growth in procedures, sales of neurosurgical products worldwide are forecasted to increase by approximately 4 percent.</font></div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In addition, the Company believes that the demand for high quality, innovative products and new technologies consistent with the Company&#8217;s devices and disposables will continue to favorably impact procedure growth in the ophthalmic and neurosurgical markets.</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Pricing Trends</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Company has generally been able to maintain the average selling prices for its products in the face of downward pricing pressure in the healthcare industry. However, increased competition, in combination with customer budget constraints, capital scarcity and the transition of procedures to the ambulatory surgery center, has continued to pressure the Company&#8217;s selling prices on these devices. The Company has no major domestic group purchasing agreements.</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Economic Trends</div>

<div>&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt">Economic conditions may continue to negatively impact capital expenditures at the hospital, ambulatory surgical center and physician level. Further, global economic conditions continue to negatively impact the volume and average selling price of the Company&#8217;s products in our European markets.</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Regulatory Developments</div>

<div>&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt">In March 2010, significant U.S. healthcare reform legislation, the Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act as modified by the Health Care and Education Reconciliation Act of 2010, was enacted into law. As a U.S.-headquartered company with significant sales in the United States, this new law will likely have a material impact on our results of operations.&#160; A number of provisions of the new health care reform legislation are not yet finalized and effective, and as such, we are unable to predict the full impact of the laws and regulations promulgated thereunder.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt">Among other matters, the law imposes a 2.3 percent excise tax on all U.S. medical device sales which became effective in January 2013.&#160; Approximately 74% of our consolidated fiscal 2014 sales were in the U.S.&#160; If we are unable to offset the taxes that will be levied on these sales, such as through the increase of efficiencies through our continuous improvement initiatives, we expect that the new tax will materially and adversely affect our business, cash flows and results of operations.</div>

<div style="MARGIN-TOP: 10pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 10pt; CLEAR: both" id="DSPFPageBreakArea">
<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: right; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', Times, Serif; FONT-SIZE: 8pt" id="DSPFPageNumberArea">31</div>

<hr style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: always; BORDER-RIGHT-WIDTH: 0px; BACKGROUND-COLOR: #000000; MARGIN: 4px 0px; WIDTH: 100%; BORDER-TOP-WIDTH: 0px; BORDER-BOTTOM-WIDTH: 0px; HEIGHT: 2px; COLOR: #000000; CLEAR: both; BORDER-LEFT-WIDTH: 0px" id="DSPFPageBreak" noshade="noshade">
<div style="WIDTH: 100%" id="DSPFPageHeader">
<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 8pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal"><a href="#TABLEOFCONTENTS">Table of Contents</a></div>
</div>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The law also focuses on a number of Medicare provisions aimed at improving quality and decreasing costs and includes provisions such as value-based payment programs and increased funding of comparative research.&#160; Furthermore, beginning in 2011, the law includes a reduction in the annual rate of inflation as used in reimbursement formulas for hospitals and the establishment of an independent payment advisory board to recommend ways of reducing the rate of growth in Medicare spending beginning in 2014.&#160; We cannot predict what healthcare programs and regulations will be ultimately implemented at the federal or state level, or the effect of any future legislation or regulation.&#160; However, any changes that lower reimbursement for our products or reduce medical procedure volumes could adversely affect our business and results of operations.</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Our Business Strategy</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Company&#8217;s key strategy is to enhance shareholder value through profitable revenue growth in targeted segments of the ophthalmology and neurosurgery markets. This is accomplished through the identification and development of reusable and disposable devices and surgical equipment in collaboration with leading surgeons and OEM partners. We are committed to establishing a strong operational infrastructure and financial foundation within which growth opportunities can be prudently evaluated, financed and pursued. We will remain vigilant and sensitive to new challenges which may arise from changes in the definition and delivery of appropriate healthcare in our fields of interest. In fiscal 2014 and beyond, our strategic priorities are to drive accelerating growth in the ophthalmology business, deliver improved profitability through our&#160;continuous improvement initiatives, manage our neurosurgery and OEM business for stable growth and strong cash flows, demonstrate consistent, solid financial performance and continued growth through strategic acquisitions.&#160; <font style="FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Enterprise-wide sales information is included in Note 17 to the consolidated audited financial statements.&#160; For additional detail on the Company&#8217;s Strategy, see Part I, Item 1, &#8220;Business &#8211; Our Business Strategy.&#8221;</font></div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Ophthalmic sales declined 0.6 percent in fiscal 2014 compared to fiscal 2013. Domestic ophthalmic sales decreased 1.3 percent primarily due to decreased sales of capital equipment and base business disposables partially offset by increased sales of VersaVIT</font><sup style="vertical-align: text-top; line-height: 1; font-size: smaller;">TM</sup><font style="FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"> procedural kits.&#160; International ophthalmic sales increased 0.2 percent primarily due to increased sales from M.I.S.S. and decreased foreign currency losses, partially offset by sales of capital equipment and base business disposables. </font>OEM sales increased by $2.2 million in fiscal 2014 as compared to fiscal 2013. Total OEM sales rose 8.3 percent to $28.7 million in fiscal 2014 (including $1.3 million of deferred revenue recognized) compared with $26.5 million in fiscal 2013 (including $1.3 million of deferred revenue recognized). The increase was primarily due to strong disposable forceps sales to Codman and strong disposable ultrasonic aspirator tips and related accessories to Stryker. Other sales decreased $25,000 in fiscal 2014, or 2.8 percent, compared to fiscal 2013.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Domestic sales increased&#160;4.1 percent in fiscal 2014 due to increases in OEM sales.&#160; The majority of OEM sales are recorded as domestic sales.&#160; The increase in international sales of&#160;0.3 percent was primarily due to the increased sales from M.I.S.S., partially offset by decreased sales of capital equipment and base business disposables.</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Gross Profit</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Gross profit as a percentage of net sales was 55.9 percent in fiscal 2014, compared to 51.5 percent in fiscal 2013.&#160; Gross profit as a percentage of net sales for fiscal 2014 compared to fiscal 2013 increased 4.4 percentage points </font>due to the following factors which occurred in fiscal 2013:&#160; (i) an approximate $1.6 million increase in the reserve for excess and obsolete inventory and its associated labor and overhead in the second quarter of fiscal 2013 impacted our margin by 2.5 percentage points; (ii) weak demand for our disposable products reduced our ability to absorb labor and overhead by 1.0 percentage point; and (iii) the decreased benefit from deferred revenue negatively impacted margin by 0.3 percentage point.&#160; Gross profit was also negatively impacted by product mix including both the products within our ophthalmology product line and the OEM sales, as they now comprise 44.3% of our sales mix.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">R&amp;D costs increased $1.5 million to $5.2 million, or 8.0 percent of net sales, for the fiscal year ended July 31, 2014, compared to $3.6 million, or 5.8 percent of net sales, for the fiscal year ended July 31, 2013.&#160; As of July 31, 2014, there were 24 active product development projects in various stages of completion.&#160; The Company&#8217;s R&amp;D investment is driven by the opportunities to develop new products to meet the needs of its surgeon customers and reflects the Company&#8217;s R&amp;D budget.&#160; This results in an investment rate that is comparable to such spending by other medical device companies.&#160; The Company expects over the next few years to invest in R&amp;D at a rate of approximately 6 to 8 percent of net sales.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Sales and marketing expenses, which consist of salaries, commissions and direct expenses, increased $555,000 to $14.4 million, or 22.2 percent of sales, for the fiscal year ended July 31, 2014, compared to $13.8 million, or 22.0 percent of net sales, for the fiscal year ended July 31, 2013.&#160; </font>The Company has added three support personnel and one marketing professional and has incurred other promotional costs as it launches the VersaVIT 2.0<sup style="vertical-align: text-top; line-height: 1; font-size: smaller;">TM</sup> vitrectomy system and related procedural kits.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Medical device excise tax increased $197,000 to $486,000, or 0.8 percent of net sales, for the fiscal year ended July 31, 2014, compared to $289,000 or 0.5 percent of net sales, for the fiscal year ended July 31, 2013 as the Company began paying the medical device excise tax in January 2013.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Exit costs were $682,000, or 1.1% of net sales, for the fiscal year ended July 31, 2014 due to the pending closure of the King of Prussia location.&#160; Exit costs consisted primarily of the severance obligations to former employees of this location.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">General and administrative (&#8220;G&amp;A&#8221;) expenses increased by approximately $49,000 during the fiscal year ended July 31, 2014 and as a percentage of net sales were 16.9 percent for the fiscal year ended July 31, 2014, as compared to 17.4 percent for the fiscal year ended July 31, 2013.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Stock-based compensation cost is measured at the grant date, based on the fair value of the award calculated using the Black-Scholes option pricing model, and is recognized over the directors&#8217; and employees&#8217; requisite service periods.&#160; The Company will continue to grant options to its independent directors and officers but uses restricted stock to provide incentive compensation for its non-officer employees.&#160; As of July 31, 2014, the future compensation cost expected to be recognized for currently outstanding options is approximately $324,000 in fiscal 2015, $238,000 in fiscal 2016, $119,000 in fiscal 2017 and $17,000 in fiscal 2018.&#160; However, the major portion of our stock compensation cost arises from our stock option grants to our independent directors, which is recognized pro-ratably over the year as the options vest.&#160; As of July 31, 2014, there was approximately $580,000 of total unrecognized compensation cost related to non-vested restricted stock-based compensation arrangements granted under the Company&#8217;s Amended and Restated 2001 Stock Plan.&#160; The cost is expected to be recognized over a weighted average period of four years, which is generally the vesting period.</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Other Income/Expense</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Other expense in fiscal 2014 decreased to $20,000 compared to other expense of $32,000 in fiscal 2013.</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Operating Income, Income Taxes and Net Income</div>

<div>&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt">Operating income for fiscal 2014 was $4.6 million, as compared to operating income of $3.7 million in fiscal 2013. The increase in operating income was primarily the result of a 6.2 percent decrease in cost of goods sold and a 3.1 percent increase in net sales (including $1.3 million of deferred revenue recognized) for a net increase in gross profit of $3.9 million.&#160; In addition, operating income was reduced in fiscal 2014 by an increase of $1.5 million in R&amp;D expenses, exit costs of $682,000, an increase of $555,000 in sales and marketing expenses, an increase of $197,000 in medical device excise tax and an increase of $49,000 in G&amp;A expenses.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt"><font style="FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">For the fiscal year ended July 31, 2014, the Company recorded a $1.5 million income tax provision on a pre-tax income of $4.6 million, or 32.8 percent effective tax rate.&#160; The effective tax rate was impacted by the expiration of the Research and Experimentation credit from December 2013 partially offset by the international tax planning the Company performed in fiscal 2014.&#160; For the fiscal year ended July 31, 2013, the Company recorded a $1.1 million income tax provision on pre-tax income of $3.7 million, or 30.6 percent effective tax rate.&#160; The effective tax rate was impacted by the re-enactment of the Research and Experimentation credit from December 2011</font>.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt">Net income increased by $504,000 to $3.1 million for the fiscal year ended July 31, 2014 from $2.6 million for the same period in fiscal 2013.&#160; Basic and diluted earnings per share from continuing operations for the fiscal year ended July 31, 2014 increased to $0.12 from $0.10 when compared to the fiscal year ended July 31, 2013.&#160; Basic weighted average shares outstanding increased to 25,323,622 at July 31, 2014 from 25,243,010 at July 31, 2013.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Ophthalmic sales grew 0.6 percent in fiscal 2013 compared to fiscal 2012. Domestic ophthalmic sales decreased 0.3 percent primarily due to decreased sales of base business capital equipment and disposables, partially offset by increased sales of VersaVIT</font><sup style="vertical-align: text-top; line-height: 1; font-size: smaller;">TM</sup><font style="FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"> vitrectomy systems and procedural kits.&#160; International ophthalmic sales increased 1.7 percent primarily due to increased sales of VersaVIT</font><sup style="vertical-align: text-top; line-height: 1; font-size: smaller;">TM</sup><font style="FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"> vitrectomy systems and procedural kits and decreased foreign currency losses, partially offset by sales of base business capital equipment and disposables. </font>OEM sales increased by $2.5 million in fiscal 2013 as compared to fiscal 2012. Total OEM sales rose 10.4 percent to $26.5 million in fiscal 2013 (including $1.3 million of deferred revenue recognized) compared with $24.0 million in fiscal 2012 (including $1.5 million of deferred revenue recognized). The increase was primarily due to strong disposable forceps and electrosurgical generator sales to Codman and strong multi-channel ablation generator sales to Stryker. Other sales increased $80,000 in fiscal 2013, or 10.0 percent, compared to fiscal 2012.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Disposable product sales accounted for approximately 80.5 percent of our total product sales in fiscal 2013.&#160; Overall sales of our disposable products grew $2.2 million, or 4.4 percent, in fiscal 2013 as compared to fiscal 2012. Sales of capital equipment increased by approximately $839,000, or 8.8 percent, in fiscal 2013 as compared to fiscal 2012.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Gross Profit</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Gross profit as a percentage of net sales was 51.5 percent in fiscal 2013, compared to 57.5 percent in fiscal 2012.&#160; Gross profit as a percentage of net sales for fiscal 2013 compared to fiscal 2012 decreased 6.0 percentage points </font>due to the following factors:&#160; (i) an approximate $1.6 million increase in the reserve for excess and obsolete inventory and its associated labor and overhead in the second fiscal quarter impacted our margin by 2.5 percentage points; (ii) weak demand for our disposables reduced our ability to absorb labor and overhead by 1.0 percentage point; and (iii) the decreased benefit from deferred revenue negatively impacted margin by 0.3 percentage point.&#160; Gross profit was also negatively impacted by product mix including both the products within our ophthalmology product line and the OEM sales, as they comprised 42.2% of our sales mix.</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">R&amp;D costs remained flat at $3.6 million for fiscal 2013 when compared to fiscal 2012.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Sales and marketing expenses, which consist of salaries, commissions and direct expenses, increased $1.9 million to $13.8 million, or 22.0 percent of sales, for the fiscal year ended July 31, 2013, compared to $11.9 million, or 19.8 percent of net sales, for the fiscal year ended July 31, 2012.&#160; </font>The Company added three territory managers and incurred other promotional costs in connection with the launching of the VersaVIT<sup style="vertical-align: text-top; line-height: 1; font-size: smaller;">TM</sup> vitrectomy system and related procedural kits.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Medical device excise tax was $289,000, or 0.4 percent of net sales, for fiscal 2013, as the Company began paying the medical device excise tax in January 2013.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">G&amp;A expenses increased by approximately $398,000 during the fiscal year ended July 31, 2013 and as a percentage of net sales were 17.4 percent for the fiscal year ended July 31, 2013 as compared to 17.5 percent for the fiscal year ended July 31, 2012.&#160; The increase in G&amp;A expenses was primarily due to stock compensation granted to directors, executive officers and senior managers of the Company in December 2012 and various other cost increases.</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Other Income/Expense</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Other expense in fiscal 2013 increased to $32,000 compared to $14,000 in fiscal 2012.</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Operating Income, Income Taxes and Net Income</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Operating income for fiscal 2013 was $3.7 million, as compared to operating income of $8.5 million in fiscal 2012. The decrease in operating income was primarily the result of a 19.3 percent increase in the cost of goods sold, partially offset by a 4.6 percent increase in net sales (including $1.3 million of deferred revenue recognized) for a net decrease in gross profit of $2.1 million.&#160; In addition, operating income was reduced in fiscal 2013 by an increase of $1.9 million in sales and marketing expenses, $289,000 in medical device excise tax and an increase of $398,000 in G&amp;A expenses.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">For the fiscal year ended July 31, 2013, the Company recorded a $1.1 million income tax provision on a pre-tax income of $3.7 million, or 30.6 percent effective tax rate.&#160; The effective tax rate was impacted by the re-enactment of the Research and Experimentation credit from December 2011.&#160; For the fiscal year ended July 31, 2012, the Company recorded a $2.5 million income tax provision on pre-tax income of $8.5 million, or 29.5 percent effective tax rate.&#160; The effective tax rate was primarily due to the favorable impact of the Company&#8217;s state tax planning strategies implemented and recorded in fiscal 2012</font>.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Income from continuing operations decreased by $3.4 million to $2.6 million for the fiscal year ended July 31, 2013 from $6.0 million for the same period in fiscal 2012.&#160; Basic and diluted earnings per share from continuing operations for the fiscal year ended July 31, 2013 decreased to $0.10 from $0.24 when compared to the fiscal year ended July 31, 2012.&#160; Basic weighted average shares outstanding increased to 25,243,010 at July 31, 2013 from 25,100,064 at July 31, 2012.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Liquidity and Capital Resources</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Company had $15.4 million in cash and cash equivalents and no interest-bearing debt as of July 31, 2014.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Working capital, including the management of inventory and accounts receivable, is a management focus. At July 31, 2014, the Company had an average of 82 days of sales outstanding (&#8220;DSO&#8221;) in accounts receivable.&#160; The 82 days of DSO at July 31, 2014 was 2 days favorable when compared to July 31, 2013 and 10 days unfavorable when compared to July 31, 2012 utilizing the trailing 12 months of sales. The DSO was impacted by the sales progression during the 2014 fourth quarter and the fiscal year.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">At July 31, 2014, the Company had 194 days of inventory on hand.&#160; The inventory on hand was unfavorable by 16 days when compared to July 31, 2013 and favorable by 30 days when compared to July 31, 2012 utilizing the trailing 12 months of cost of sales.&#160; The Company had invested approximately $3.7 million in inventory for new products and new product launches at the end of fiscal 2014.&#160; However, the Company had $2.2 million in backlog as of July 31, 2014.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Cash flows provided by operating activities were $5.7 million for the year ended July 31, 2014, compared to cash flows provided by operating activities of approximately $3.7 million for the comparable fiscal 2013 period.&#160; The improvement in cash flows of approximately $2.0 million </font>was primarily attributable to the decrease in accounts receivable of $2.1 million, the decrease in deferred taxes of $1.9 million and $0.9 million in various other adjustments. This increase was partially offset by a decrease in accounts payable of $1.7 million and decrease in accrued expenses of $1.2 million.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Cash flows used by investing activities were $2.6 million for the year ended July 31, 2014, compared to cash used by investing activities of $3.8 million for the comparable fiscal 2013 period.&#160; During the year ended July 31, 2014, the Company invested $1.4 million in the acquisition of a private OEM company.&#160; During the year ended July 31, 2013, the Company invested $2.8 million net cash in the acquisition of M.I.S.S.&#160; In addition, during the year ended July 31, 2014, cash additions to property and equipment and patents were $0.9 million and $0.3 million, respectively, compared to $0.5 million and $0.4 million for fiscal 2013, respectively.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Cash flows provided by financing activities were approximately $0.1 million for the year ended July 31, 2014, compared to cash provided by financing activities of $0.1 million for the year ended July 31, 2013.&#160; The Company received proceeds of $59,000 and a $38,000 income tax benefit from the exercise of stock options compared to proceeds of $65,000 and a $72,000 income tax benefit for fiscal 2013, respectively.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Company had the following committed financing arrangements as of July 31, 2014:</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Revolving Credit Facility: </font>The Company has a credit facility with a bank which allows for borrowings of up to $9.5 million with an interest rate based on either the one-, two- or three-month LIBOR plus 1.75 percent and adjusting each quarter based upon our leverage ratio. As of July 31, 2014, interest under the facility is charged at 1.98 percent. The unused portion of the facility is charged at a rate of 0.20 percent. There were no borrowings under this facility at July 31, 2014. Outstanding amounts are collateralized by the Company&#8217;s domestic receivables and inventory. This credit facility was amended on September 30, 2013, to extend the termination date through September 30, 2016.</div>

The facility restricts the payment of dividends if, following the distribution, the fixed charge coverage ratio would fall below the required minimum.</div>

Pursuant to the terms of the equipment line of credit, under no circumstance shall the rate be less than 3.5 percent per annum. The unused portion of the facility is not charged a fee. There were no borrowings under this line as of July 31, 2014. The equipment line of credit was amended on September 30, 2013 to extend the maturity date to September 30, 2016.</div>
